nodes.summary: MULTIWAY CUT is the decision problem on bitstrings that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a multiway cut instance $(n, E, T, K)$ that is well-formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to a multiway cut instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The MULTIWAY CUT decision problem

nodes.summary: Let $(n, E, T, K)$ be a multiway cut instance with terminal list $T = (t_0, \dots, t_{k-1})$. It is feasible when there is a labelling $f$ of the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ by labels in $\{0, \dots, \max(k, 1) - 1\}$ such that $f(t_j) = j$ for every $j < k$, and at most $K$ entries $(u, v)$ of $E$, counted with repetition, satisfy $f(u) \ne f(v)$. Here every number $v \ge n$ counts as a vertex with label $0$.
nodes.title: Feasible multiway cut instances

nodes.summary: A multiway cut instance is a tuple $(n, E, T, K)$ consisting of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edges), a list $T$ of natural numbers (the terminals) and a natural number $K$ (the bound on the number of cut edges).
nodes.title: Multiway cut instances

nodes.summary: Let MULTIWAY CUT be the decision problem that accepts exactly the bitstrings decoding to a well-formed, feasible multiway cut instance: a simple undirected graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, a list of distinct terminal vertices and a bound $K$ such that deleting at most $K$ edges of the graph leaves no two terminals connected. Then MULTIWAY CUT is in NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to MULTIWAY CUT…
nodes.title: MULTIWAY CUT is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A multiway cut instance $(n, E, T, K)$ is well-formed when the entries of $E$ are pairwise distinct; every entry $(u, v)$ of $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and $(v, u)$ is not an entry of $E$; the entries of $T$ are pairwise distinct; and every entry $t$ of $T$ satisfies $t < n$. Thus $E$ lists each edge of a simple undirected graph on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ exactly once, in one orientation,…

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
